description: Get rug-check token contract security and liquidity risk signals, and the Rug Check score the /rug-check page shows, computed by the API: score.value (0-100, higher is safer; null only when no pillar had a scorable figure), score.verdict, score.data_completeness and score.engine_version, with the checks[] behind it.

chainId.description: EVM chain ID (1 Ethereum, 56 BNB Smart Chain, 8453 Base, 42161 Arbitrum, 137 Polygon, 10 Optimism, 43114 Avalanche, 146 Sonic, 80094 Berachain, and 29 more), or 1399811149 for Solana and 728126428 for Tron. An unsupported chain returns 400.

name: get_rug_check_security

RugCheckCheck.description: One row of the /rug-check page's Checks table.

pillar.description: The pillar the row scores under: `contract` (weight 0.40), `holders` (0.35: the wallets' share among the token's top 10 holders, GoPlus's live list without the token's own pools and burn addresses, or GeckoTerminal's snapshot when GoPlus has none) or `health` (0.25, market figures).

status.description: `neutral`: shown without a judgement (unknown, or an owner-only power of a renounced contract).

liquidity.description: The pool's value in USD from GoPlus: Solana's pool TVL, and on EVM chains twice GoPlus's one-sided figure for a UniswapV2-type pool. Null when GoPlus gives no comparable figure: EVM concentrated-liquidity pools (UniswapV3/V4, whose GoPlus figure is not the pool's value) and pools it sends without one.

lpBurnedShare.description: Burned share of this pool's LP tokens, 0 to 1 (0.7837 is 78.37%), from GoPlus, counting destroyed LP and LP held in Raydium's lock. Solana standard AMM pools only: null for concentrated-liquidity pools and on EVM chains.

RugCheckScore.description: The Rug Check score the /rug-check page shows for this token, computed server-side (engine metric token_risk.rug_check) from this answer's GoPlus fields, the token's DexScreener market figures (liquidity and 24h volume summed over its pairs on this chain, age from its oldest pair) and its top-10 holder share (GoPlus's live top-holder list without the token's own pools and burn addresses; GeckoTerminal's snapshot when GoPlus has none, ignored when stale). Weighted 0.40 contract, 0.35 holders, 0.25 market health, then capped by hard signals (a honeypot or sell block sets 5, a copy of a major's ticker from another contract 49). An input a lookup could not read is unknown, never zero: it is left out of its pillar's average (its row reads `—`), a pillar with no data at all scores a neutral 50, and `data_completeness` says whether every pillar had data; a `partial` score is capped at 69. On a `stale` answer the score is computed from the last good GoPlus record. Present on every 200 answer.

data_completeness.description: `full`: the contract, holder and market pillars each had data. `partial`: one or two had none (each such pillar scores a neutral 50, and the score is capped at 69 so unknown data never reads `safe`). `none`: no pillar had a scorable figure (a holder count alone scores nothing), so there is no score.

engine_version.description: Version of the scoring rules. A declared change to a weight, cap, band or check increments it, so a stored score can be told apart from one computed under other rules.

insights.description: The verdict's reasons as the page lists them, at most 6.

value.description: 0-100, higher is safer. Null only when no pillar had a scorable figure (`data_completeness` `none`), never a default 50.

verdict.description: `safe` at 80 or more, `caution` at 50, `risky` at 20, else `danger`. Null when `value` is null.

verdict_label.description: The verdict as the page labels it. Null when `value` is null.

verdict_note.description: "Trusted issuer, centralised controls" when GoPlus trust-lists the token and its issuer can still mint, freeze, pause or upgrade it: those controls are listed as warnings but neither scored nor capped. Otherwise null.

checks.description: The rows of the /rug-check page's checks for this token, in the page's order: the Contract Security rows, then the Top-10 holders row, then the Token Health rows. Present on every 200 answer, beside `score`.

dataAsOf.description: When the last good record was fetched. Present only alongside `stale`.

dexInfo.description: DEX pools, deepest first by `liquidity` (pools with a null `liquidity` last), so entry 0 is the main pool when its value is known.

holderCount.description: Wallets holding the token: the count the `Holders` check shows, GeckoTerminal's holder snapshot or GoPlus's count when that snapshot is stale or missing. On a `partial` record, null.

lpHolders.description: LP holders of the main pool (the deepest dexInfo entry). Each holder's `share` is its part of that pool's LP token supply, 0 to 1 (0.0002 = 0.02%) on every chain; Solana shares are recomputed from the holder balance over the pool's LP amount. Null when the list cannot be tied to a standard AMM pool.

partial.description: Present and true only when the security provider was unavailable and the token has no last good record, on Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain or Base: `isHoneypot` comes from Honeypot.is's buy/sell simulation and every other security field is null (unknown). The score then treats the contract checks as unknown, except that a detected honeypot scores 5 (Danger). Absent otherwise.

stale.description: Present and true only when the security provider was temporarily unavailable and this is the token's last good record (at most 7 days old). Absent on live answers.

meta.description: Which route answered, what the API said about the data's freshness, and whether the client cut the answer to fit the agent's context window.

route.description: Always `v1`: every call reads the keyed /v1 route.

truncated.description: True when the answer is cut short: by the API's row budget, or by the client (`truncated_fields`).

truncated_fields.description: The arrays and strings the client cut, by JSON path in `data`: `total` items received, `showing` kept, `kept: latest` when an oldest-first series kept its newest items.

warnings.description: What the API or the client could not do, in words. State them with the answer.

pagination.description: Present when the answer is one page: pass `cursor` back to read the next one.
